Emphasizes its use in military applications but also mentions civilian applications.
Mentions cooling high-temperature superconducting (HTS) devices and shares an example of using these coolers for measuring adult heart signals.

activities.description: Discussing ongoing research on reducing the size of cryogenic coolers.
Showing and explaining a prototype of a Joule-Thomson cryocooler, and research on regenerative cooler cycles.

scenes.contextualRelevance: Prof. ter Brake discusses research developments in cryogenic coolers.

narrativeProgression.description: Introduction to the research aim of miniaturizing cryogenic coolers.
Focus on Joule-Thomson micro cryocooler, highlighting its use in combination with absorption compressors.
Introduction of a prototype Joule-Thomson cooler working with ethylene and reaching 170K in one stage.
Explanation of micromachining techniques used for creating a check valve with minimal dead volume to improve efficiency.
Introduction of research on regenerative cooler cycles, using pulse tubes or Stirling type coolers, and exploration of new regenerative materials.

props.name: A complex laboratory setup with a large metal container, various tubes, wires, and a cooling fan.
A slide with a diagram and text 'Micromachined Joule-Thomson cryocooler' and a close-up view of the cooler.
A slide with a diagram and text 'Joule-Thomson micro cryocooler' and a close-up view of the cooler.
A slide with a diagram and text 'Sorption cooler.'
A slide with a diagram and text '165 K demonstrator: cold stage' and a photo of a small metal device with wires.
A close-up of a small black device labeled '50T' attached to a gold-colored block.
A close-up shot of a large metal device with two cylindrical tubes protruding from it, then a close-up of a transparent tube and a yellow cylindrical device with a metal cap on each end.
Close-ups of hands filling the transparent tube with small white, flat circular objects.

activities.description: Explaining the challenges and potential solutions related to regenerative cooler materials, focusing on heat capacity and phase transitions.

scenes.contextualRelevance: The discussion highlights advancements and challenges in materials science related to cryogenic cooling.

narrativeProgression.description: Introduction of the graph showing specific heat capacity against temperature.
Comparison of lead (Pb) and helium (He) as regenerative materials, highlighting the decrease in lead's heat capacity and the increase in helium's heat capacity at lower temperatures.

Explanation of the need for materials with higher heat capacity than lead at low temperatures, highlighting the potential of rare earth nickel alloys (ErNi, Er2Dy0.8Ni2) due to their magnetic transitions and phase transitions.

props.name: A hand-drawn graph on a blue grid background illustrating specific heat capacity (kJ/m³K) against temperature (K) for various materials.
